body:
Confirmed from the affected session: with `/etc/ca-certificates` added to the sandbox read list, the symlinks resolve and TLS works with no environment override.

```
$ readlink -f /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
/etc/ca-certificates/extracted/tls-ca-bundle.pem
$ curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://api.github.com
200
$ gh api user --jq .login
Nemo-010
$ git ls-remote https://github.com/QaidVoid/errand HEAD
6a62f91f25f5c5b6498a753b768db4c8b623dcd2	HEAD
```

This grant was added as a session `policyExtra` read entry, so the built-in `SYSTEM_READ` list in `src/sandbox/policy.ts` still omits `/etc/ca-certificates` and every other Arch-family deployment hits the same failure by default. The one-line default fix from the report stands.

Fixed on `main` in 7a24e121. The diagnosis was exactly right: `SYSTEM_READ` granted `/etc/ssl` but not the tree the Arch symlinks point into, so they dangled inside the session.

Your report said this only affected the Arch family, and that turned out not to be quite true. Probing the canonical bundle path across the current images:

```
archlinux     /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt -> /etc/ca-certificates/extracted/tls-ca-bundle.pem
tumbleweed    /etc/ssl/ca-bundle.pem             -> /var/lib/ca-certificates/ca-bundle.pem
fedora        /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt -> /etc/pki/ca-trust/extracted/pem/tls-ca-bundle.pem
alpine        /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt  REAL FILE
```

openSUSE fails the same way, for the same reason, and nobody had hit it yet. Fedora is fine as you said, since `/etc/pki` was already granted. So the list now covers both:

```ts
  "/etc/ssl",
  "/etc/ca-certificates.conf",
  "/etc/ca-certificates",
  "/var/lib/ca-certificates",
  "/etc/pki",
```

Naming a path that is absent on a given host is already how this list works. `/etc/pki` does not exist on the Gentoo box I tested on, has been listed in every generated policy there, and those sessions run fine, so all four families can be named at once without a per-distro branch.

There is a regression test in `src/sandbox/policy_test.ts` asserting all four reach the generated policy.

Your `policyExtra` workaround can come out once you are on this commit. Thanks for the report: the `readlink` output and the `SSL_CERT_FILE` check isolated it precisely enough that there was nothing left to guess at.
